finding: The paper stores episodic observations, reflections, and plans as natural-language memory-stream records associated with time and importance; retrieval favors records using recency, relevance, and importance signals.
scope_limit: The simulator's character/world memory is not a measured capability profile or a reusable general problem-solving method.

finding: The paper describes reflections synthesized from accumulated memories after an importance threshold; these are additional natural-language records used in later planning and retrieval.
scope_limit: The inspected paper does not establish reflection as a revision to the method that produces or evaluates reflections.

mechanism: Expiration field in pinned Generative Agents code
finding: ConceptNode stores an expiration field and serializes/deserializes it; the code path also initializes last_accessed from created. This establishes a field, not a running expiration, deletion, or semantic freshness policy.
scope_limit: The local inspection did not read saved simulation records or trace every consumer of expiration; no expiry behavior is inferred from the field alone.

finding: The paper separates read-only system instructions, bounded writable working context, a FIFO message queue, and external archival/recall storage. Function calls move selected information between context levels.
locator: §§2.1-2.3, especially lines 71-89 in the versioned HTML
scope_limit: The mechanism extends usable context and retrieval; it does not itself demonstrate a revised cognition method or calibrated self-model.

mechanism: MemGPT queue eviction and recall retention
finding: On overflow, the paper describes evicting queue messages and generating a recursive summary; the evicted messages remain readable from recall storage and are described as stored indefinitely.
locator: §2.2 Queue Manager, lines 77-82 in the versioned HTML
scope_limit: This describes the paper's design and retention behavior, not the current Letta Code product implementation.

finding: The paper makes memory edits and retrieval available as functions guided by system instructions; the processor decides when to move or edit information, while the runtime parses and executes validated calls.
locator: §2.3 Function executor, lines 83-89 in the versioned HTML
scope_limit: A writable memory tool is bounded by its function contract; self-directed memory editing is not proof that the edit method itself changes.

finding: The pinned Letta Code snapshot defines a per-agent memory root under ~/.letta/agents/{id}/memory and resolves an explicit agent/runtime scope before environment fallbacks.
scope_limit: This is an implementation snapshot, not evidence that every Letta deployment uses the same backend or config.

finding: The pinned code lists persona and human as default memory block labels and marks configured read-only blocks before loading defaults; a comment says skills are injected by system reminders in this version.
scope_limit: Prompt-bound memory content can shape behavior, but this file does not define an independent capability-profile or method-inheritance mechanism.

finding: Memory patches require a nonempty reason and structured operations, validate the target path and scope, reject read-only files, and commit accepted writes with agent identity. In memfs-v2, MEMORY.md indexes cannot be deleted or moved.
scope_limit: This provides accountable memory mutation and structural constraints; no independent semantic evaluator of each memory fact was found in the inspected paths.

finding: The pinned code documents clone-on-first-run, pull-on-startup, commits for memory writes, and post-turn pushes of pending commits. Memory lives in a Git-backed per-agent repository in the inspected paths.
scope_limit: This is static source evidence; no user memory repository was accessed and no runtime sync was invoked.

finding: The pinned validator defines per-file character, core-memory character, and directory-depth caps; changing its tracked config is blocked unless the explicit environment override is set, and the error text says not to raise or disable limits without explicit user approval.
scope_limit: These are size/scope limits and an approval gate, not semantic deduplication, forgetting, or a quality guarantee.

finding: Local compaction summarizes evicted conversation messages and retains a recent sliding window or replaces the buffer with a summary. This is context-window management, distinct from semantic long-term memory retirement.
scope_limit: A summary used to continue a local conversation is not evidence that stored memory has been validated, retired, or propagated to a successor model.

finding: No explicit TTL, revalidation-on-model-change, or evaluator-backed invalidation policy for a capability/self-knowledge profile was found in the inspected Generative Agents, MemGPT paper, or Letta Code paths. MemGPT memory pressure and Generative Agents timestamps are different mechanisms.
locator: Bounded source review listed in source-freeze.jsonl; compare GenAgents ConceptNode fields with MemGPT §§2.1-2.3 and Letta Code memory-constraints/compaction paths
scope_limit: This is an absence claim limited to the frozen artifacts and inspected paths, not a claim about all deployments or all product features.

finding: Persistent and retrievable memory can alter later prompts and actions, but the reviewed systems do not show a measured transfer of the method that selects, validates, consolidates, or retires memories to a different successor model.
locator: Crosswalk synthesis over the cited paper sections and pinned code paths
scope_limit: This conclusion is about evidence inspected here; it does not deny the practical utility of persistent memory or prompt conditioning.
